explain.say: Some things are really hard to say out loud, even to someone who loves you. That is okay, and there are ways to make it easier. Look at the first step on the board: pick your adult, someone who listens and helps.

explain.say: Look at this feelings meter. Before telling, the needle often points to scared, and your heart thumps. That is normal. The tools help: breathe, write a note, bring a friend with you, or call a helpline.

explain.say: And after telling, most people feel lighter, see the calm zone? If nothing changes, tell another adult, and keep telling. You are brave just for learning this. You never have to carry a hard thing alone.

faq.q: How do I start telling an adult something hard?
faq.a: Start simple: I need to tell you something, it is important. Or: Can we talk? Something is worrying me. The adult will help with the rest.

faq.q: What if I cannot find the words?
faq.a: Write a note, draw a picture, or text it. You can even say: It is hard to talk about, can I write it down?
asks: Tell me about the Write or draw it

faq.q: Is it normal to feel scared to tell?
faq.a: Yes, very normal. Your body might shake or your heart might race. Being scared and telling anyway is what bravery means.
asks: What if I am scared to tell a teacher?

faq.q: What if the adult does not help?
faq.a: Tell another trusted adult, and keep telling until someone does. You can also call a free child helpline.

faq.a: A parent or carer, a grandparent, aunt or uncle, a teacher, a school counsellor, a doctor or nurse, or a child helpline.

facts: Child Helpline International links free helplines for children in more than 130 countries, many open by phone and online chat.
Counsellors often suggest children write a note if saying something difficult out loud feels too hard.

quiz.say: You want to tell your teacher something hard but cannot find the words. What could you do?

options.show: Write a note and give it to them
options.say: Write a note and give it to them

quiz.why: A note is a great way to tell when talking is hard.

wrong.1: Keeping it inside can make it feel heavier.
wrong.2: Hard things often do not go away without help.

quiz.say: You told an adult, but nothing changed. What next?
quiz.why: Keep telling until someone helps you.

wrong.0: There are other adults who will help.
